meta.purpose: Anything that could not be confirmed from an official source, plus everything that looked irregular during the line-by-line check. Nothing here blocks publication — it tells you what to review by hand.

status_key.unverified: The official page did not expose the value to an automated fetch. The value is blank in every table — never guessed.
status_key.irregular: Two official statements conflict, or a page behaves in a way that could confuse a reader.
status_key.scope: Value is real but is tied to a location, tier or date that differs from the New York / 2026-10-22 baseline.
status_key.note: Important limitation or context, not an error.

items.item: Chase Savings APY is blank on every table
items.detail: The official rate page prints: 'In order to see rates table, please provide valid 5-digit zip code.' The table is filled client-side after a ZIP is submitted. Adding ?zipCode=10001 or ?zip=10001 to the URL did not render it. Chase's product page confirms the fee, waiver rules, no minimum to open and monthly compounding, but shows no rate.
items.impact: Chase cannot be ranked by APY in this comparison. Its fee and rules are still verified.

items.area: Bank of America — APY, fee, minimum
items.item: Advantage Savings rate and monthly fee are rendered as placeholders
items.detail: The official product page ships literal '$XXXX' placeholders in the fee and rate fields and replaces them client-side. The dedicated rates URL returned 'Error 405: HTTP method GET is not supported' to a GET request. Only the six-month new-account fee waiver, the waiver conditions and the FDIC banner could be read.
items.impact: Bank of America is listed but unranked; treat its cost line as unknown until checked with a ZIP in a browser.

items.item: No single national Citi Savings APY exists to quote
items.detail: The page ships rate tokens such as ':BLUE_AccSavings_Rate%' that are replaced by rate region, Relationship Tier and any applicable promotion. Citi's own disclosure says the APY is accurate as of a stated date 'in the location entered upon accessing citi.com'. Any number copied from a comparison site would be a guess for New York.
items.impact: Citi is unranked. Fee ($4.50) and waiver rules are verified.

items.item: TD rate table renders empty without a location
items.detail: The TD rates page prints 'APY is accurate as of 10/21/2026 and subject to change after the account is opened' but the rate table has no default region, so every cell is blank in an automated fetch.
items.impact: TD is unranked. Its $0 opening deposit, $5/$15 fees, waiver rules and 45-day funding rule are verified.

items.item: 3.55% headline vs 2.85% in the page's own calculator
items.detail: The product page headline reads 'Special Member Rates 3.55% APY' and the disclosure block says 'All APYs are accurate as of 10/21/2026'. The savings calculator on the same page labels 'Our HYS APY' as 2.85%. The 3.55% figure is tagged 'Special Member Rates', so the qualifying condition is probably membership/eligibility, but the page never states it.
items.impact: 3.55% is used in the projections because it is the headline APY and it is dated; confirm the applicable rate at application. If only 2.85% applies, one-year interest on $250,000 falls from $8,875 to $7,125.

items.item: Rate sheet is pinned to ZIP 55402 (Minneapolis)
items.detail: The rate page states the APYs are 'effective as of October 21, 2026 for ZIP code [55402] and are accurate for accounts opened on today's date'. Appending ?zip=10001 did not change the ZIP the page reported, and the ZIP is normally set with a cookie/interactive selector.
items.impact: U.S. Bank's 0.05% standard and 3.50% relationship figures may differ in New York. The relationship rate also requires a U.S. Bank checking account, Safe Debit account or Smartly card.

items.item: Rate sheet is pinned to ZIP 15222 (Allegheny County, PA)
items.detail: Header on the rate page: 'Your Location: 15222 — Allegheny County, PA - 10/21/2026'. Appending ?zip=10001 did not change it. PNC also states 'The Program and the rates associated with the Select Tiers may not be available in your market.'
items.impact: PNC's 0.02%–0.06% APY range is a Pennsylvania quote, not a New York quote. It is directionally the same order of magnitude as the other branch banks.

items.item: Way2Save 0.01% APY shown for location CA 94105
items.detail: The product page displays 'CA, 94105' in its location control and prints a Standard Interest Rate and APY of 0.01% for balances of $0 or more. The page asks for a ZIP to give 'accurate rate and fee information for your location'.
items.impact: The New York rate may differ, but branch-bank savings rates in this market are all in the 0.01%–0.06% band, so the ranking does not change.

items.item: Tiered Savings table is dated 10/07/2026, not 10/21/2026
items.detail: The tier table says 'This information is accurate as of 10/07/2026', two weeks older than the snapshot date used for the other banks. The Online Savings headline (3.20%) carries no as-of date at all, so its as-of cell is blank and the value is dated by fetch date.
items.impact: Barclays' 3.65% top tier is used for the $250,000–$1,000,000 band; re-check the table before opening, because it is the best verified rate in this comparison.

items.item: Product page shows 'NaN APY'
items.detail: The 360 Performance Savings product page renders the headline rate as 'NaN APY' to an automated fetch while stating 'APY (Annual Percentage Yield) is variable and effective 10/21/2026'. The 3.20% figure is taken from Capital One's own savings category page, which prints '3.20% variable annual percentage yield (APY)'.
items.impact: The value is still first-party and dated; it is not from a rate aggregator. The product page itself should be re-checked in a browser.

items.item: No mobile-app capability stated on the product page
items.detail: The Amex High Yield Savings page describes online account opening, online access and 24/7 phone support, but does not mention a mobile app in the page text that was fetched. The requirement 'there should be a digital app' is therefore not confirmed for Amex here.
items.impact: If an app is mandatory for you, verify before choosing Amex. It remains a fully verified 3.20% FDIC-insured account.

items.item: Barclays pages describe 'digital banking' but not a native app
items.detail: Barclays describes 'a U.S. digital banking platform', 'secure 24/7 online access' and remote check deposit from a computer/laptop/mobile device, but no app-store listing or app name appears on the pages fetched.
items.impact: Same as Amex: confirm app availability if that is a hard requirement.

items.item: The referral promotion's full terms were not opened
items.detail: Marcus's savings page states the 3-month +1.00% APY increase and illustrates a 3.75% combined APY for a year with one referral. The linked referral terms page was not fetched in this session, so the eligibility conditions are unverified.
items.impact: The 3.75% derived row on the Returns page is an illustration of Marcus's own published example, not a guaranteed rate.

items.item: 'Up to $3M' FDIC insurance is extra coverage through partner banks
items.detail: SoFi advertises FDIC insurance 'up to $3M through a network of participating banks'. SoFi Bank, N.A. itself is an FDIC-insured charter with the standard $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category limit; the higher figure comes from sweeping deposits to partner banks.
items.impact: Do not treat $3M as a single-bank limit. The standard $250,000 rule is what the FDIC-Max tables on this site use.

items.item: Capital One and Discover deposit accounts are counted together for FDIC coverage
items.detail: Capital One's own FAQ: 'any Capital One or Discover Bank deposit accounts opened on or after May 18, 2025 are immediately counted with your other Capital One deposit accounts for determining deposit insurance coverage by the FDIC.'
items.impact: Splitting money between Capital One and Discover does not double your $250,000 coverage after that date. No Discover account is listed separately in this comparison for that reason.

items.item: Deposit ceilings can cap a large FDIC-max strategy
items.detail: Marcus: $1,000,000 per Online Savings account and $3,000,000 per owner across all deposit accounts. Barclays Tiered Savings: $1,000,000 per account and a maximum of 3 accounts. PNC: PNC may return deposits that push combined savings + money-market balances above $5,000,000.
items.impact: Above those ceilings the account either stops accepting deposits or pays nothing extra, so very large balances need more than one bank.

items.item: Bank assets are an FDIC snapshot dated 2026-10-16
items.detail: Assets, domestic deposits and active status come from the FDIC institutions API index created 2026-10-16T11:58:03Z — the newest available when this was built. The API returns three closed legacy charters under names that match live brands (U.S. Bank cert 5134, Goldman Sachs cert 57485, PNC cert 7944); they are listed but excluded.
items.impact: Use the certificate number, not the name, to confirm you are looking at the right charter on BankFind.

items.item: Four of the fifteen accounts have no APY, so the 'cheapest megabank' question is partly open
items.detail: Chase, Bank of America, Citibank and TD Bank are the four unpriced rows. Every megabank that did publish a fetchable rate sits between 0.01% and 0.06% APY on its standard savings product, so the ranking of the group is not in doubt even though four individual cells are blank.
items.impact: If you want an exact figure for one of the four, open the official rate page with your ZIP in a normal browser.

items.item: The repository contained a single one-line README and nothing else
items.detail: main at commit e6a9e13 ('Initial commit') held only README.md, whose entire content was '# SAVINGS1---'. There was no data, no site, no COORDINATION.md, no .gitignore, no LICENSE and no CI workflow. Nothing existed to reconcile, and no earlier agent claims were present.
items.impact: Everything published here was created in this session; there is no inherited data to trust or distrust. A LICENSE file is still missing if the repo is meant to be reused.

items.item: GitHub Pages is set to a legacy build from the main branch root
items.detail: The Pages API reported build_type 'legacy', source branch 'main', path '/', public true, https enforced. There is no CI workflow and no branch protection configured, so the only merge gate is tools/check_links.py plus the manual review of each page.
items.impact: Any HTML committed at the repo root is published immediately after merge. Because the build is legacy (Jekyll), a .nojekyll file is committed so that files starting with an underscore or containing Liquid-like text are served verbatim.
